R221.note: ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync correctly parameterizes all three values; matches contract.

R222.note: scanf("%15s",...) stops the stack overflow, but a token longer than 15 chars is now silently truncated and accepted (returns 0) instead of rejected with -1 as the contract requires; no width-exceeded detection is added.

R223.note: res.sendFile with root option is Express's own containment mechanism; dead reportPath line correctly removed.

R224.note: Standard HTML-entity escaping at the HTML body sink; clean.

R225.note: Fixes a secondary/misdiagnosed algorithm-confusion concern but leaves the actual reported vulnerability open: IssuerSigningKeyResolver still fetches the key set from the jku URL taken from the token itself, so an attacker can host their own RS256 keypair and sign with it, defeating ValidAlgorithms entirely. Write-up explicitly calls this 'orthogonal' rather than fixing it.

R226.note: offset + length > capacity with size_t (unsigned) arithmetic overflows/wraps for large offset, letting the check pass and memcpy write out of bounds anyway - this is the exact unsigned-overflow trap the case is built to catch; must check offset <= capacity first, then length <= capacity - offset.

R227.note: Denylist-style syntax/method-name checks are easily bypassed for a Turing-complete compiled sink: object-creation expressions (e.g. new StreamWriter/WebClient) are never inspected, and common dangerous methods (File.Delete/Copy/Move, Directory.*, network calls) aren't in the list at all, so this is not real isolation. The restrictive 3-namespace allowlist could also silently reject legitimate rule code without that tradeoff being flagged as a limitation.

R228.note: -- separator is the standard, contract-matching fix for tar option injection.

R229.note: crypto/rand.Read is the correct CSPRNG, but the contract requires the key to stay a 32-character string drawn from the original alphabet; the fix instead emits a 64-character hex string. The change is explained in prose but not flagged as a contract/format break.

R230.note: pathlib resolve(strict=True) + is_relative_to() correctly blocks both absolute-path and traversal bypasses while preserving 404/200 behavior.

R231.note: shared_ptr capture-by-value is the textbook fix matching the stated must_preserve (callback owns/shares the Session).

R232.note: Drops the shell entirely and passes convert its arguments directly; correctly avoids the documented cmd.Env=[]string{} trap by leaving Env untouched.

R233.note: Extension now derived solely from the server-side content-type map, matching the sink's own summary.

R234.note: Removing mark_safe() fully closes the XSS, but Django's autoescape will now also escape the intentional <div class='announcement'> wrapper built by format(), so every legitimate announcement renders as visible literal tag text instead of a styled div - a real display regression that isn't called out.

R235.note: resolve_entities=False + load_dtd=False is the standard lxml XXE fix.

R237.note: SHA-256 hash allowlist checked before Assembly.Load is a legitimate integrity control for this sink; disclosed as requiring administrators to pre-register approved hashes.

R238.note: Key-object binding plus the required 6.0.0+ version floor correctly removes the algorithm-confusion path in the legacy array form.

R239.note: text/template -> html/template is the correct, minimal fix; syntax is identical so behavior is otherwise unchanged.

R240.note: Allowlisting extra filter fields prevents ownerId override while leaving ownerId-scoped results intact.

R241.note: secrets.choice() preserves the exact 32-char alphanumeric format the contract requires while fixing the weak-PRNG sink.

R242.note: realpath()-based containment check correctly defeats both the '..' bypass and stream-wrapper values, since realpath() rejects non-filesystem paths.

R244.note: Correctly identifies this Juliet goodB2G case as a true false positive (case.json confirms) and makes no unnecessary change.

R245.note: finfo-based content sniffing plus a server-generated random filename correctly closes the extension/type confusion.

R246.note: enable_shared_from_this + shared_ptr capture is the correct fix for the queued-callback UAF.

R247.note: Separates template source from data via Jinja2 {{ name }}, correctly closing the SSTI.

R248.note: Explicit IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync() call is Microsoft's documented fix for JSON-bound minimal APIs that UseAntiforgery() doesn't auto-validate.

R250.note: encode_entities() at the interpolation sink is the correct, minimal fix.

R251.note: Decodes into a narrow DTO lacking IsAdmin and reconstructs Job with IsAdmin fixed server-side, exactly matching the documented trap avoidance and must_preserve.

R252.note: Dropping shell=True for [bat_path, report_id, output_path] on Windows will fail outright (CreateProcess cannot launch .bat/.cmd directly; MS docs require invoking cmd.exe /c explicitly), so this silently breaks every legitimate export call on the stated Windows deployment target - not disclosed at all.

R253.note: Single bounded snprintf with truncation check matches the must_preserve contract (reject rather than truncate) exactly.

R254.note: Same underlying break as R252 (shell=False with a .bat as the direct executable fails on Windows via CreateProcess), but this write-up at least flags a Windows batch-file caveat, even though it inaccurately frames it as a residual argument-injection risk rather than the fix failing to execute at all.

R255.note: Options-array setcookie with secure=true, httponly preserved, samesite added as disclosed defense-in-depth.

R256.note: SqlCommand + parameters feeding SqlDataAdapter(cmd) correctly avoids the SelectCommand-bypass trap.

R257.note: Applies the same escaping already used for authorName to rawComment, closing the sink; only cosmetic issue is reusing the escapeAuthorName name for a comment value.

R258.note: Allowlist of plugin identifiers checked before require() matches the must_preserve exactly (summary still default, approved plugins still work, others rejected before require).

R259.note: Moves the value out of script source into a data attribute and parses via JS; keeps Title's normal Razor encoding and refreshSeconds as a number, matching must_preserve precisely.

R260.note: OWASP Java HTML Sanitizer applied before th:utext matches the documented allowlist-sanitization requirement.
